chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who belches, so something comes out from him, should he repeat the wudu? He (peace be upon him) said: No.
ai.seo_question: Does belching break wudu in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'najasah' (impurity) is carefully distinguished from mere 'fasad' (breaking of wudu), establishing that belching does not invalidate ritual purity unless accompanied by the exit of substantial matter. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'istishab al-taharah' (presumption of continued purity), requiring clear evidence to overturn the default state of cleanliness. It serves as a foundational precedent for distinguishing between minor bodily functions and those that necessitate full ablution renewal.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al’ala who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who belched, so something came out from him, ‘Should he repeat the Ablution (Wudhu)?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Husayn ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who belches and something comes out in his mouth. Is he required to take Wudu’ again?’
He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not necessary for him to take Wudu’”
